title: Margin-space slice discovery beats embedding-space clustering
one_line_idea: Discover error slices by clustering examples in the geometry of logit margins and loss trajectories rather than in penultimate-layer embedding space.
problem: Standard slice discovery clusters failures in a feature embedding, which groups examples by appearance similarity rather than by why the model fails on them.
core_hypothesis: Clusters formed in margin/loss-dynamics space align better with actionable failure causes (fixable by one intervention) than clusters formed in embedding space.
core_claim: Clusters formed in margin/loss-dynamics space align better with actionable failure causes (fixable by one intervention) than clusters formed in embedding space.
method_sketch: On one classifier and one detector, cluster errors both ways, apply per-slice targeted fine-tuning with matched budgets, and compare fraction-of-slice-repaired distributions across the two geometries.
falsifiable_prediction: For matched cluster counts, a single targeted fine-tuning intervention per slice repairs a larger fraction of margin-space slices than embedding-space slices on the same model and dataset.
why_important: If slice geometry should be defined by model behavior rather than input appearance, most current slice-discovery pipelines are optimizing the wrong space.
why_possibly_novel: Loss-trajectory features are used for data valuation, but using them as the primary clustering geometry for slice discovery and validating slices by repair success is not something I can point to as established; novelty unverified.
novelty_hook: Loss-trajectory features are used for data valuation, but using them as the primary clustering geometry for slice discovery and validating slices by repair success is not something I can point to as established; novelty unverified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On one classifier and one detector, cluster errors both ways, apply per-slice targeted fine-tuning with matched budgets, and compare fraction-of-slice-repaired distributions across the two geometries.
main_risk: Margin dynamics may be too noisy per example, making margin-space clusters unstable across seeds and no more actionable than embedding clusters.
kill_risk: Margin dynamics may be too noisy per example, making margin-space clusters unstable across seeds and no more actionable than embedding clusters.
community_default_belief: Penultimate-layer embeddings are the right space in which to cluster failures because they capture semantic similarity.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Semantic similarity of inputs is not the same as similarity of failure mechanism; two visually similar images can fail for unrelated reasons.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: Cluster one model's errors in both spaces and simply measure within-cluster agreement of a cheap cause proxy (e.g., which augmentation flips the prediction); if embedding clusters agree as often, the idea dies.

title: Intervention-validated captions for auto-named slices

title: Hierarchical slice trees with parent-repair inheritance

kill_risk: Repair transfer may be dominated by shared label noise or dataset artifacts rather than genuine causal hierarchy, producing an uninterpretable tree.

fastest_falsifying_experiment: Fine-tune on one parent slice's data and check three child slices versus three distant slices; no transfer gradient kills the tree premise.

title: Separating model-wrong from label-wrong slices by design

kill_risk: Diverse models may share biases (similar pretraining data), so consensus against the label can still indicate correlated model error rather than label error.

title: Ensemble disagreement today forecasts next year's model errors

title: Fixability scoring: predicting whether a slice will respond to retraining

title: Consensus-audit estimation of label-error share in mined failures

title: Instruction ambiguity as a mineable error source
one_line_idea: Identify error slices traceable to underspecified annotation instructions, then fix the instructions, re-annotate the slice, and measure how much 'model error' disappears.

title: Anchoring bias in model-assisted error audits

title: Do user-reported failure modes match feature-space slices?
